text:
Ava: quick follow-up from today's all-hands pricing section. dropping a thread for clarifications on credits, rate limits, and grace bursts.
Rohit: thanks. quick customer Q: during a demo we burned credits much faster than the calc suggested. any pointers for estimates on streaming heavy chat flows?
Maya: streaming is token-billed: prompt + streamed response + tool outputs. we also see extra per-request overhead for many tiny streams. best practice: batch where possible or use longer streams instead of many short ones.
Diego: can we give a concise example? customers love numbers.
Maya: example: prompt 150 tokens, stream 600 tokens => ~750 billable tokens. if price is $0.0008/token -> ~$0.60. we'll add a calc widget to KB.
Kenji: ops: repeated reconnects can trigger a small health-check quota and be throttled; healthcheck endpoints are exempt from billing but still count against that tiny quota.
Rohit: policy: what happens on route-rate exceed? 429s only?
Ava: default self-serve: 429 + Retry-After header. Dedicated can opt into short queuing (configurable up to 10s) or fallback to cheaper model variants on overflow.
Maya: graceburst note: small automatic graceburst available once per billing period for accounts in good standing; it consumes credits and is not a free allowance. larger bursts require Support request.
Diego: SDK behavior on 429s? headers?
Kenji: SDKs include Retry-After and x-rw-quota-token. they also emit a client event 'rate_limit.hit'. we're adding a helper for jittered exp backoff in the next SDK milestone.
Ava: actions: Maya to publish KB with examples tomorrow, Kenji to add SDK backoff helper item to sprint, product to mock credits overlay in Console.
deploy-bot: KB stub posted: https://intranet.redwood/KB/credits-graceburst-stub
Rohit: will ping when KB is live. drop follow-ups here.
